title: Adaptive Safety Net: Threshold Sculptor for Canary & Shadow Traffic
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current canary and shadow deployments rely on static numeric thresholds for latency, error-rate, token-cost and throughput. This leads to brittle rollouts (false positives during traffic surges, missed regressions in tail latency, and cost blindspots). We need a runtime-aware, adaptive trigger composer that fuses multiple signals, normalizes token-cost impact, and sculpts hysteresis bands so rollouts can safely advance and retreat without manual tuning.

Goal: Implement an "Adaptive Safety Net" feature (threshold sculptor) that generates and continuously tunes rollback triggers for canary/A-B/shadow traffic using multi-signal fusion, cohort baselining, and traffic-aware hysteresis. Triggers should be explainable, auditable, and expose tunable knobs in Console. Provide a lightweight simulation mode and a rollout advisor that suggests initial thresholds per model family and region.
acceptance_criteria: Safety Net composes rollback triggers from at least four signals: p95 latency, error rate (>=5xx and user-facing errors), normalized token cost delta, and sustained throughput change
Adaptive thresholds update at runtime using rolling-window baselines and cohort-aware deviation scoring (no manual patch deployments required)
Canary rollouts with Adaptive Safety Net enabled automatically pause or rollback when composite score crosses configurable band; Console shows breakdown and "why" explanation for each action
Simulation mode produces >90% fidelity against historical incidents in the synthetic test harness (benchmarks attached)
Rollout advisor provides recommended initial bands per model family and returns guidance in Console and via API
Feature flag gated; default off for existing customers; telemetry includes explainable events and links to trace/span ids
implementation_notes: Signal fusion: compute z-scores per metric over sliding windows, then weight by signal importance (latency=0.4, error=0.35, cost=0.15, throughput=0.1 default)
Cost normalization: convert delta token cost into a per-request z-score using recent usage distribution to detect anomalous per-token inflation
Hysteresis bands: graduated bands (warning, hold, rollback) with configurable dwell time to avoid flip-flopping under transient load
Cohort baselining: baseline metrics per traffic cohort (region, customer tier, model-size) and compute cohort-relative deviations
Explainability: persist composition reasons (top contributing signals) for every triggered action and surface in Console and incident logs
APIs: expose /rollout/advisor and /rollout/simulate endpoints and add metadata to existing rollout objects
Storage: compact time-series summaries (quantiles, count, mean) instead of raw per-request logs for real-time scoring
Backwards compatibility: when disabled, Conservative fallback to existing static threshold logic
testing_plan: Unit tests for z-score computation, weight adjustments, and hysteresis state machine
Synthetic harness: replay traffic traces (normal, surge, gradual regression, cost drift) to validate expected decisions
Canary lab: end-to-end test in dedicated staging with mirrored shadow traffic and intentional regressions
A/B experiment: enable Adaptive Safety Net for 5% of internal traffic for 7 days and compare false-positive/negative rates against baseline
Chaos tests: simulate delayed metrics, partial telemetry loss, and sudden throughput spikes to confirm stable decisions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (feature dev): implemented behind feature flag; internal-only; simulation mode available (ETA 2026-03-22)
Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 10 internal canaries; monitor for 2 weeks; iterate on weighting and dwell times
Phase 2 (beta): expose to limited customers with opt-in; Console advisory only (no automatic rollback) for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (GA): automatic rollback enabled by default for dedicated deployments with conservative defaults and opt-out
Rollback to original static thresholds available via Console toggle; safety kill-switch in control plane
risks: Overfitting weights to internal workloads may underperform on customer traffic—mitigate by cohort baselining and A/B experiments
Telemetry delays could cause incorrect early rollbacks—implement dwell windows and require multiple consecutive windows for action
Cost-normalization errors could mute cost regressions for rare heavy hitters—add a direct token-cost alert channel and per-customer sensitivity setting
UI complexity: too many knobs may confuse customers—provide curated advisor presets and 'recommended' mode
